purpose: Curated artistic briefs, twenty representative subjects and finished comparisons. Paths are relative to this file; old generation/run records are intentionally omitted.

items.name: Apples
items.depiction: Two red-green apples, one whole and one clean cut half showing seeds.
items.tests: Familiar fruit and a cut surface.

items.name: Eggs
items.depiction: Two brown eggs, one intact and one broken shell with its yellow yolk visible.
items.tests: Small rounded objects and fragile shell.

items.name: Flour
items.depiction: A small open cloth sack of fine matte off-white flour, a soft powder mound at its mouth.
items.tests: Fine powder; compare sugar.

items.name: Sugar

items.name: Cooked chickpeas

items.name: Milk

items.name: Cream

items.name: Whipped cream

items.name: Pouring custard

items.tests: Flowing sauce; distinguish pastry cream.

items.name: Pastry cream

items.name: Dough
items.depiction: A simple soft pale raw dough ball with a folded seam, uncooked and not a baked loaf.
items.tests: Raw dough surface.

items.name: Laminated dough

items.tests: Raw folded layers.

items.name: Puff pastry

items.tests: Baked expansion and crisp flaky edges.

items.name: Ginger root
items.depiction: A knobbly fresh ginger root with one freshly cut pale yellow face; no leaves.
items.tests: Irregular root silhouette.

items.name: Coriander leaves
items.depiction: A small bunch of fresh coriander/cilantro with delicate lobed green leaves and visible thin stems, loosely tied.
items.tests: Fine leaves and stems.

items.name: Soy sauce
items.depiction: A tiny shallow white ceramic dish of very dark glossy brown soy sauce, with a thin amber meniscus at its edge; no bottle or label.

items.name: Whisk
items.depiction: One complete metal balloon whisk with an ordinary wooden handle and clearly separated wire loops, diagonally placed.
items.tests: Thin tool structure and a long silhouette.

items.name: Rolling pin
items.depiction: One complete long plain wooden rolling pin with two handles, lying almost horizontally at a slight diagonal.
items.tests: Very wide object; a strong varying-size test.

items.name: Bean stew and soda bread
items.depiction: A bowl of reddish-brown bean stew with visible beans and vegetables, alongside a rustic soda-bread wedge showing dense crumb; one small meal grouping.
items.tests: A finished meal with several components.

items.depiction: An empty practical two-shelf wooden kitchen serving trolley, curved push handle and four small wheels, both shelves visible. No food on it.
items.tests: Large compound base; fittings are deferred.

directions.name: Traditional painted game icons
directions.medium: Polished traditional hand-painted adventure-game inventory art. Convincing materials and rounded volumes, clear edges, restrained warm highlights, moderate detail, consistent shallow three-quarter viewpoint. Friendly old-fashioned kitchen craft. NOT mobile-game plastic, not a flat vector symbol. Use the supplied traditional-game sheet only as a reference for foreground painting. Do NOT paint its scenic background or circular backing into this atlas; those will be added in the contact-sheet layout.
directions.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: food icon contact sheet for a comparative art-direction study, a gently twee travelling-cook story.
Composition: Make one landscape contact-sheet atlas containing EXACTLY twenty separate subjects in a strict invisible 5-column by 4-row grid. Prefer 2000 x 1600 pixels (5:4 aspect). Each equal cell contains exactly one numbered-list subject, in the listed row-major order. Centre each complete subject within its cell; keep a generous empty margin of at least 15% on every side of every cell, and all silhouettes and shadows away from cell boundaries. Similar maximum extent in every cell, except naturally long thin objects keep their aspect ratio. No overlaps across cells. GENUINELY TRANSPARENT background throughout the empty space. No text, labels, numbers, grid lines, frames, borders or backing disks. No surrounding scenes, hands or people. Do not add unlisted ingredients as identity cues. Contents and preparation states matter. No duplicated or missing subjects. We will crop and arrange these cells in a comparison gallery; later display sizes are chosen outside this source atlas.
Style/medium: Polished traditional hand-painted adventure-game inventory art. Convincing materials and rounded volumes, clear edges, restrained warm highlights, moderate detail, consistent shallow three-quarter viewpoint. Friendly old-fashioned kitchen craft. NOT mobile-game plastic, not a flat vector symbol. Use the supplied traditional-game sheet only as a reference for foreground painting. Do NOT paint its scenic background or circular backing into this atlas; those will be added in the contact-sheet layout.
Subjects in exact order, five across each row:
1. Apples: Two red-green apples, one whole and one clean cut half showing seeds.
2. Eggs: Two brown eggs, one intact and one broken shell with its yellow yolk visible.
3. Flour: A small open cloth sack of fine matte off-white flour, a soft powder mound at its mouth.
4. Sugar: A shallow plain bowl of white granulated sugar with a few distinct crystalline grains beside it.
5. Cooked chickpeas: A shallow plain bowl of plump cooked golden chickpeas with clearly recognizable individual shapes.
6. Milk: A simple transparent glass milk bottle filled with thin white milk; open top, no label.
7. Cream: A small simple open ceramic cream jug with a visible smooth ivory liquid surface and a short spout.
8. Whipped cream: A shallow plain bowl holding soft white whipped cream in airy irregular peaks, not ice cream or frosting rosettes.
9. Pouring custard: A small sauce jug of pale yellow custard with a spoon held close over the opening and a thin flowing ribbon returning into the jug.
10. Pastry cream: A shallow bowl of thicker pale yellow pastry cream, with a firm spatula ridge holding its shape; no dripping.
11. Dough: A simple soft pale raw dough ball with a folded seam, uncooked and not a baked loaf.
12. Laminated dough: A squat rectangular folded slab of raw laminated dough; three broad folded layers visible at the cut side, pale, unbaked.
13. Puff pastry: One baked rectangular puff-pastry piece, golden brown with expanded flaky layers and a small broken corner revealing the airy interior.
14. Ginger root: A knobbly fresh ginger root with one freshly cut pale yellow face; no leaves.
15. Coriander leaves: A small bunch of fresh coriander/cilantro with delicate lobed green leaves and visible thin stems, loosely tied.
16. Soy sauce: A tiny shallow white ceramic dish of very dark glossy brown soy sauce, with a thin amber meniscus at its edge; no bottle or label.
17. Whisk: One complete metal balloon whisk with an ordinary wooden handle and clearly separated wire loops, diagonally placed.
18. Rolling pin: One complete long plain wooden rolling pin with two handles, lying almost horizontally at a slight diagonal.
19. Bean stew and soda bread: A bowl of reddish-brown bean stew with visible beans and vegetables, alongside a rustic soda-bread wedge showing dense crumb; one small meal grouping.
20. Supper trolley: An empty practical two-shelf wooden kitchen serving trolley, curved push handle and four small wheels, both shelves visible. No food on it.
Critical distinctions: raw folded dough is pale and dense; baked puff pastry is golden, expanded and flaky. Cream is liquid; whipped cream has airy peaks. Pouring custard flows; pastry cream holds a ridge. The trolley is EMPTY. Flour, milk, cream and soy sauce need not be falsely identifiable without their normal names. Preserve real material cues. Draw twenty complete separate subjects and keep all empty areas truly transparent.

directions.name: Big, cartoony mobile-game icons
directions.medium: Exuberant premium casual mobile cooking-game art: chunky exaggerated proportions, plump simplified volumes, saturated appetizing colours, bold clean silhouette, smooth 3D cartoon shading, generous bright highlights and tactile toy-like finish. Strongly cartoony, visibly more exaggerated than traditional inventory paintings. Objects only, no eyes or faces, no UI badges, coins or stars.

directions.name: Grounded tempera still lifes
directions.medium: Grounded naturalistic egg-tempera food illustration. Observed believable proportions; matte layered small brush marks; restrained natural pigments; tactile flour, wood grain, linen, cream and flaky pastry; precise but gently softened edges. Quiet warm daylight and modest three-quarter depth. The mood is a real cook's useful equipment in a welcoming travelling kitchen, not toy objects, not glossy 3D, not sepia nostalgia.

directions.name: Cook's pen notebook
directions.description: Scratchy pen and restrained washes; a loose carrot-and-herb vignette above open paper, with a softly fading bottom. Physical proportions and a 60 px minimum.
directions.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make lively, genuinely DRAWN observational food studies, like the pen sketches in the reference. A quick irregular black fountain-pen line, sometimes a second searching contour, a little crosshatching, broad EMPTY WHITE interiors and only one or two flat yellow-ochre or moss accents. Much more drawing than painting. Some subjects side-on, others overhead; lopsided vessels, awkward handles, unpolished proportions, beautifully casual. A student drawing real things at their kitchen table, not an illustrator rendering inventory. No smooth volume, no gradients, no realistic material shading, no glossy highlights, no detailed grain or 3D food.
The supplied references are for artistic vocabulary and marks, not to reproduce their specific compositions or lettering. Twenty subjects, in exactly this row-major order: row 1: apples (one whole, one cut); eggs; flour; granulated sugar; cooked chickpeas. Row 2: milk; liquid cream; whipped cream; pouring custard; thick pastry cream. Row 3: raw dough; folded laminated dough; baked puff pastry; ginger; coriander leaves. Row 4: dark soy sauce; a long balloon whisk; a long rolling pin; bean stew with soda bread; a small two-shelf serving trolley. Show the whisk and rolling pin almost horizontally, very long and thin. Food may be shown from above, the side, partly cropped within its own depiction, in unusual bowls or as an expressive shape. No identical stock-vessel convention.
Deliver an ARTWORK SHEET arranged as five columns by four rows, one separate study per cell, with clean generous gaps so the studies can later be composed into a freeform cookbook page at wildly different sizes. The grid is only a delivery format. Keep each whole drawing, including its loose paint splashes, inside its cell. Transparent outside the drawing and its intentional paint marks; white food and reserved white parts can remain white. No labels, no type, no outlines around cells. Start afresh, not from our previous icon sheets.

directions.prompt:

Pigment goes well outside the outlines in places and leaves much of the object white in others. Cobalt, turquoise, rose pink, yellow ochre and juicy orange; unexpected violet shadows. Blooms, accidental backruns, transparent puddles, a few splashes, unfinished bits. Spontaneous five-minute sketches. A flour bowl can be five pen curves and a pink wash. An apple can be one looping outline and a wet red blot with a green splash. directions.name: Lightbox photorealism
directions.description: Isolated photorealistic objects with soft white-lightbox lighting, authentic textures and modest 60–112 px variation.
directions.prompt:
Create a production atlas of TWENTY isolated photorealistic food and kitchen objects: imagine a meticulous high-end food/product photographer has photographed each real object separately inside a large WHITE LIGHTBOX, then supplied clean transparent cutouts. NOT rectangles of lifestyle photography: no kitchen, no tabletop, no linen, no room, no scene or cropped-off objects. The objects themselves should look convincingly photographic, not painted, not cartoon, not 3D-rendered toys. Soft large studio lights, realistic glass transparency and reflections, metal highlights, food pores and tiny imperfections, appetizing true textures; deep focus across each entire object. Very faint short contact shadow allowed; empty surroundings must be transparent alpha.
Compose EXACTLY 5 columns by 4 rows, evenly spaced, twenty separate subjects, each centred wholly inside its own cell with generous empty gutters. Row-major order:
ROW 1: (1) a real red apple with a cut half beside it; (2) two whole eggs and a cracked egg with visible yolk; (3) flour in a plain off-white ceramic bowl with a small powder mound; (4) granulated white sugar in a small clear glass jar, distinct visible crystals; (5) cooked chickpeas in a small plain bowl.
ROW 2: (6) milk in a clear glass jug; (7) liquid cream in a little white ceramic pouring jug; (8) freshly whipped cream with soft irregular peaks in a mixing bowl; (9) pouring custard: a spoon held above a bowl with a continuous flowing yellow ribbon, the complete bowl and complete spoon visible; (10) thick pastry cream holding a ridge in a bowl.
ROW 3: (11) a plain unbaked dough ball; (12) folded RAW laminated dough with pale butter-and-dough layers visible; (13) one modest rectangular portion of BAKED puff pastry with golden airy layers; (14) knobbly ginger root with two slices; (15) a small bunch of fresh coriander with complete stems.
ROW 4: (16) dark soy sauce in a shallow white dipping dish; (17) a stainless balloon whisk nearly horizontal; (18) a wooden rolling pin horizontal, BOTH handles fully visible; (19) a rustic bowl of bean stew with a piece of soda bread beside it as one group; (20) a real small wooden two-tier kitchen serving trolley, complete wheels and handles, empty shelves.
Use restrained practical crockery and authentic objects. No typography, logos, badges, boxes, circles, borders, scenery, lens blur or props other than specified. No overlaps between cells. This atlas will be separated into independent draggable objects on a cookbook page, with modest size variation applied afterwards. Preserve delicate whisk wires and clear jug edges. TRANSPARENT background.
